prompts.a: Let $f$ be the function given by $f(x)=\frac{Ax}{x^2+B}$, where $A$ and $B$ are positive constants. The function $f$ has a critical point at $x=3$, and $f(3)=3$. Find the values of $A$ and $B$.
prompts.b: For the values of $A$ and $B$ found in part (a), find $\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)$. Then give an equation for the horizontal asymptote of the graph of $y=f(x)$.
prompts.c: Show that $f$ has an absolute maximum value of $3$ and an absolute minimum value of $-3$ on the interval $-\infty<x<\infty$. Justify your answer.
prompts.d: For which values of the constant $k$ does the equation $f(x)=k$ have exactly two solutions? Justify your answer.

prompts.a: A sealed capsule holds $120$ grams of a radioactive tracer. Let $M(t)$ be the mass of the tracer, in grams, remaining $t$ years after the capsule is sealed. The rate at which the mass decreases is proportional to the mass present, so $\frac{dM}{dt}=-kM$ for a positive constant $k$. Use separation of variables to find an expression for $M(t)$ in terms of $k$.
prompts.b: The half-life of the tracer is $5$ years, that is, $M(5)=\frac12 M(0)$. Find the value of $k$.
prompts.c: At what time $t$ will $12$ grams of the tracer remain? Express your answer in terms of natural logarithms.
prompts.d: Find the average mass of the tracer in the capsule over the time interval $0\le t\le 10$ years. Give your answer in grams, in exact form.

input.design_note: Parts keep all given numbers and math blocks; wording only lightly polished (part b now asks for the value of k), and the four parts build from deriving M(t) to k, a time to a given mass, and an average value.

prompts.d: On the closed interval $-1\le x\le 2$, find the $x$-coordinate of the absolute maximum and the $x$-coordinate of the absolute minimum of $f$. Justify your answers.

prompts.a: A farmer builds a rectangular pen against a long stone wall, so no fence is needed along the wall. The pen has area $150$ square meters and is divided into two stalls by one more fence perpendicular to the wall. Fence perpendicular to the wall costs $6$ dollars per meter, and the fence opposite the wall costs $12$ dollars per meter. Let $x$ meters be the length of each fence perpendicular to the wall. Write an expression for the total cost $C(x)$, in dollars, of the fence in terms of $x$ only.
prompts.b: Find the value of $x$ for which $C'(x)=0$.
prompts.c: Use the second derivative of $C$ to justify that the value of $x$ found in part (b) gives the absolute minimum cost over all possible values of $x$.
prompts.d: Find the minimum total cost, in dollars, and the length, in meters, of the fence opposite the wall for that pen.

prompts.b: Let $g$ be the function defined by $g(x)=\frac{x^3-1}{\ln x}$ for $x>0$ with $x\ne 1$, and $g(1)=c$. For what value of $c$ is $g$ continuous at $x=1$? Justify your answer.

prompts.a: A workshop makes and sells $q$ hundred custom phone cases per week, for $0\le q\le 10$. The marginal revenue is $MR(q)=18-2\ln(q+1)$ and the marginal cost is $MC(q)=2+0.2q^2$, both in thousands of dollars per hundred cases. Find $MR(2)-MC(2)$. Using correct units, explain what this value says about the profit when production is increased from $q=2$.
prompts.b: The profit is $P(q)=R(q)-C(q)$, where $R$ and $C$ are the revenue and cost functions. Find the production level $q$ that gives the maximum profit on $0\le q\le 10$. Justify your answer.
prompts.c: Find the increase in total revenue, in thousands of dollars, when production is raised from $q=2$ to $q=6$ hundred cases. Show the setup for your calculation, including the definite integral you use.
prompts.d: The weekly fixed cost is $6$ thousand dollars, so $P(0)=-6$. Find the profit at the production level found in part (b). Does the workshop make a profit or a loss at that level? Justify your answer.

input.design_note: Parts connect marginal analysis, optimization via MR=MC with a sign-change justification, a definite integral of MR for the revenue increase, and the net change of MR-MC added to P(0) for the optimal profit.

prompts.a: A drainage trench is dug along a straight line for $20$ meters. prompts.b: The area function is modeled by $A(x)=16+5\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{6}\right)$ for $0\le x\le 20$. Use the model to find the volume of the trench. Show the setup for your calculation. (A calculator may be used for the integral; give your answer to three decimal places.)

prompts.a: During a charging test, the current into a small battery is modeled by $I(t)=4e^{-t/4}\sin(0.8t)$ amperes (coulombs per second), where $t$ is the time in seconds and $0\le t\le 8$. The net charge delivered to the battery during the first $x$ seconds is $Q(x)=\int_0^x I(t)\,dt$ coulombs. Find $Q(3)$ and $Q'(3)$. Show the setup for any integral you evaluate.
prompts.b: Find the average rate of change of $Q$ over the interval $2\le x\le 7$. Using correct units, explain what this average rate of change represents in the context of the problem.
prompts.c: For $0\le x\le 8$, at what value of $x$ does $Q$ attain its absolute maximum value? Find that maximum value and justify your answer. Show the setup for any integral or equation you solve.
prompts.d: On which open intervals within $0<x<8$ is the graph of $Q$ concave up? Give a reason for your answer.

input.design_note: All four parts rest on Q(x) = integral of I(t) from 0 to x. They test evaluating the accumulation function, the Fundamental Theorem (Q' = I), an average rate with units, a candidate-and-endpoint test for the absolute maximum, and concavity from the sign of I'.
